rituals.name: SHOELACE START

rituals.rule: Guess whether the tiniest physical start changes motivation even one point.

rituals.twist: Look for any change after motion begins rather than before.

rituals.name: CROSS THE DOORWAY
rituals.goal: Move your body into the task zone before your brain holds another meeting.
rituals.mission: Move your body into the task zone before your brain holds another meeting.
rituals.rule: Guess whether crossing one physical boundary will make the task feel more real or more impossible.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether crossing one physical boundary will make the task feel more real or more impossible.

rituals.name: FIVE-SECOND CHOICE LOCK
rituals.goal: For one reversible choice, the parliament gets five seconds.
rituals.mission: For one reversible choice, the parliament gets five seconds.
rituals.rule: Guess whether choosing quickly feels worse than continuing to hover.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether choosing quickly feels worse than continuing to hover.
rituals.play: Pick a low-stakes reversible decision. Count 5–4–3–2–1. At one, choose A or B and physically begin it. No reopening for 60 sec.
rituals.twist: Check if discomfort comes from the choice—or from losing the option to keep deciding.
rituals.mindBend: A reversible choice rarely needs the emotional certainty of a permanent one.
rituals.mind_bend: A reversible choice rarely needs the emotional certainty of a permanent one.
rituals.why: Indecision can feel safer because every option remains imaginary and untested.

rituals.goal: Avoidance gives relief now and sends the invoice later.
rituals.mission: Avoidance gives relief now and sends the invoice later.
rituals.rule: Guess the relief you get tonight and the extra cost tomorrow, each from 0–10.

rituals.recognition_cue: Future temptation expected to overpower current intention
rituals.unique_game_move: LOCK IN BEFORE THE MOOD ARRIVES
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Create a mild reversible commitment in advance that increases the friction of abandoning a planned behaviour during a predictable future temptation state.
rituals.ritualText:
PLAY TIME
70 sec

GAME
LOCK IN BEFORE THE MOOD ARRIVES

GOAL
Decide while the persuasive future mood is not in the room.

ONE RULE
Guess which choice future-you is most likely to bargain away.

PLAY
Choose one reversible commitment now: book the slot, prepare the food, block the site, place the item, tell someone the time, set the alarm. Make later avoidance slightly harder.

TWIST
Notice the difference between deciding in a calm state and renegotiating inside temptation.

MIND BEND
You do not have to out-argue future temptation if you redesign the meeting.

SAFETY
PAUSE
If another person is part of the commitment, keep it voluntary and proportionate; informing them is not permission to make them responsible for your follow-through.

rituals.name: HALF THE CONTAINER
rituals.goal: A giant time window can turn a small task into fog.
rituals.mission: A giant time window can turn a small task into fog.
rituals.rule: Guess what would happen if you had half as long as usual.
rituals.one_rule: Guess what would happen if you had half as long as usual.
rituals.play: Take a routine task you know reasonably well. Give it a realistic but tighter window—about half the casual buffer, not half the necessary work.
rituals.twist: Notice which low-value behaviours disappear first.
rituals.mindBend: More time can create more work without creating more value.
rituals.mind_bend: More time can create more work without creating more value.
rituals.why: Available time shapes how much process accumulates around a task.
rituals.reveal: Available time shapes how much process accumulates around a task.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: DISTRACTION CAN WAIT TEN
rituals.goal: You do not have to defeat the distraction.
rituals.mission: You do not have to defeat the distraction.
rituals.rule: Guess whether the urge will still feel equally urgent in ten minutes.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether the urge will still feel equally urgent in ten minutes.
rituals.play: When the distraction appears, schedule it for ten minutes later instead of banning it. Put the exact time somewhere visible.
rituals.twist: Check if 'later' creates less rebellion than 'never.'
rituals.mindBend: An urge can be postponed without becoming a moral battle.
rituals.mind_bend: An urge can be postponed without becoming a moral battle.
rituals.why: Short delays can weaken impulsive choice without demanding permanent denial.
rituals.reveal: Short delays can weaken impulsive choice without demanding permanent denial.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Let this pass interrupt an ordinary habit loop, not override a basic need or medical instruction. Stop if delaying the urge creates risk. If the same pattern returns later, re-check the new context rather than copying today's answer.

rituals.goal: Effort can become less unpleasant when it repeatedly leads somewhere.

rituals.mind_bend: Your brain can learn that effort is a path, not only a cost.
rituals.why: Effort can acquire secondary rewarding properties through reinforcement history.

rituals.name: REWARD MARKET AUDIT
rituals.goal: Your schedule says priority.
rituals.mission: Your schedule says priority.
rituals.rule: Guess which option gives faster, more frequent little payoffs: useful work or distraction.

rituals.twist: Check if behaviour allocation starts making behavioural sense.
rituals.mindBend: Your attention may be following the better-paying environment, not the better intention.
rituals.mind_bend: Your attention may be following the better-paying environment, not the better intention.
rituals.why: Response allocation tends to track relative rates of reinforcement.
rituals.reveal: Response allocation tends to track relative rates of reinforcement.

PAUSE
